content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Redundant wording in ORR endpoint",
      "quote": "compared with compared with investigator’s choice of SOC",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'compared with' is duplicated, which is a typographical error that could cause confusion in the endpoint definition.",
      "fix": "Remove the duplicate 'compared with' to read 'compared with investigator’s choice of SOC'."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent tumor tissue submission requirement",
      "quote": "must also be submitted within 2 weeks of enrollment for confirmation of RET status by central testing",
      "page": 45,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring submission within 2 weeks of enrollment may be logistically challenging and could lead to protocol amendments if sites cannot meet this timeline, especially for fresh biopsies or when shipping delays occur.",
      "fix": "Consider extending the submission window or allowing submission before enrollment with central confirmation as a post-enrollment activity."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ambiguous exclusion for CNS metastases",
      "quote": "Participant has either CNS metastases or a primary CNS tumor that is associated with progressive neurological symptoms or requires increasing doses of corticosteroids to control the CNS disease.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "5.2",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The criterion is ambiguous because it does not specify whether stable CNS metastases without progressive symptoms are allowed, which could lead to inconsistent interpretation and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Clarify that participants with treated and stable CNS metastases are eligible if asymptomatic and not requiring increasing corticosteroids."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing safety monitoring for RET inhibitor class",
      "quote": "To evaluate the safety and tolerability of pralsetinib compared with investigator’s choice of SOC platinum-containing anticancer treatment regimens",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoints listed are generic (AEs, ECOG, vital signs, labs) and do not include specific monitoring for known pralsetinib toxicities such as hypertension, hepatotoxicity, and interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, which are class effects of RET inhibitors.",
      "fix": "Add specific safety monitoring endpoints for hypertension, liver function tests, and pneumonitis, and include corresponding assessments in the Schedule of Activities."
    },
    {
      "title": "Restrictive prior therapy exclusion may limit enrollment",
      "quote": "Participant cannot have received any prior anticancer therapy for metastatic disease.",
      "page": 45,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This criterion is standard for first-line trials but may be overly restrictive if some patients have received prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease that is not RET-targeted, potentially limiting enrollment and generalizability.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing prior therapy if it was not a selective RET inhibitor and if the patient has not progressed on it, or justify the restriction in the protocol."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent contraception duration for men",
      "quote": "during the treatment period and for 7 days after the final dose of pralsetinib",
      "page": 45,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 7-day post-dose contraception duration for men is shorter than the typical 90 days recommended for cytotoxic agents, and may be inconsistent with the SOC platinum regimen requirements, potentially leading to confusion.",
      "fix": "Align the male contraception duration with the SOC labeling or extend to a more standard period (e.g., 90 days) for consistency."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing safety monitoring for pembrolizumab-containing regimen",
      "quote": "Participants who have received previous immune checkpoint inhibitors in the adjuvant setting or consolidation therapy following chemoradiation are not allowed to receive pembrolizumab if randomized to Arm B.",
      "page": 45,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify additional safety monitoring for participants receiving pembrolizumab (e.g., immune-related adverse events, thyroid function, adrenal insufficiency), which is a known safety concern for checkpoint inhibitors.",
      "fix": "Add specific safety monitoring for immune-related AEs and endocrine function for participants on pembrolizumab."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ambiguous tumor tissue requirement for cell pellet",
      "quote": "if tumor tissue cannot be obtained, a fixed and embedded cell pellet from pleural effusion would be acceptable for central confirmation of RET fusion status",
      "page": 45,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The acceptability of a cell pellet is not clearly defined in terms of adequacy criteria, which may lead to variability in sample acceptance and potential enrollment delays.",
      "fix": "Define specific adequacy criteria for cell pellet samples (e.g., cellularity, tumor cell content) in Section 8.10."
    }
  ]
}
